_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated (formative: automatically when the student clicks Generate; assessed: only via the ?teacher=1-gated action, after Final Submit). Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md §5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least one of their OWN logged days (a setting value and the sugar made, e.g. light 10 percent gave about 10 units) AND states clearly whether this result supports or contradicts the hypothesis they locked in before testing.
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine logged day from the student's own Investigation Record showing sugar fall when one setting was turned down, paired with any judgement (supported, contradicted or partly supported) that is consistent with that data.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('the sugar went down') with no actual figures from their own Record, or no judgement made against their hypothesis.

markingScheme.criterion: Names the setting that cut the sugar and states what photosynthesis uses it for (light supplies the energy, water is a reactant delivered by the xylem, carbon dioxide is a reactant that enters through the open stomata).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement linking the named setting to its role in photosynthesis, in the student's own words. Light, water or carbon dioxide is acceptable provided the role is correct.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the setting is 'important' or 'needed' with no role given.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that with too little of that ingredient photosynthesis slows down (it is the limiting factor), so less glucose is made, even if the other ingredients are plentiful.
markingScheme.accept: Any scientifically valid phrasing of the limiting-factor idea, e.g. the scarcest ingredient sets the pace. Exact keywords are not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating 'less light so less sugar' without saying why the missing ingredient stops the reaction from running at full speed.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies the phloem as the tube damaged (it lives in the inner bark, so the wire cut it) and says it carries sugar DOWN from the leaves.
markingScheme.accept: Phloem named, with sugar or food moving down. Accept 'the inner bark tubes that carry sugar' if the word phloem is missing but the job is clear.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming the xylem, or saying only 'the bark' with no mention of sugar or food moving down.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the bulge: sugar made in the leaves cannot pass the wire, so it piles up above the ring and the trunk swells there.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that sugar or food is trapped above the cut.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the tree 'grows more' above the wire with no mention of sugar being stuck.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that roots below the wire starve because roots cannot make their own sugar and no sugar can reach them, while the leaves still look healthy because the xylem inside the wood still lifts water.
markingScheme.accept: Roots depend on sugar delivered from the leaves AND the cut does not stop water rising. Either clearly stated half plus a correct explanation of why roots starve is enough for this mark.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the roots starve with no reason, for example because they cannot get sugar.

levels.descriptor: Achieves none of the three: no own logged day quoted with a hypothesis judgement, no role given for the setting, and no limiting-factor explanation.
Achieves only ONE of the three points.
Achieves TWO of the three points, for example quotes their own day with a hypothesis judgement and names the role of the setting, but does not explain that the scarce ingredient limits the rate.
Quotes their own logged day with a hypothesis judgement, names the role of the setting in photosynthesis, and explains that too little of it slows sugar-making. All three points present.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: Achieves none of the three: phloem not identified, no explanation of the bulge, no explanation of why the roots starve.
Achieves only ONE of the three: for example names the phloem and says it carries sugar down, but cannot explain the bulge or the starving roots.
Achieves TWO of the three: for example names the phloem and explains the bulge, but gives no reason the roots starve.

Names the phloem and the downward sugar flow, explains the bulge as sugar piling up above the wire, and explains that the roots starve because they cannot make sugar and none reaches them. All three present.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together, independent of and never overlapping with the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Hard to follow, or key vocabulary is missing or incorrect.
Understandable, but with unclear phrasing or a missing or misused term.
Clear, full sentences across both answers using correct terms such as xylem, phloem, stomata, photosynthesis, glucose.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and does not count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points. The rubric levels restate the same points as bands, so award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (7 marks = full). Use the student's own logged days (the light/water/stomata/sugar/limit columns in simulation_results.trials) to verify any figure they quote. Do not take their prose summary on trust if it does not match their logged data. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 15 (7 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report the percentage, one strength, one correction, and one next step, in under 80 words.
